Commentary.Commentary: We are back with England's say with the bat in hand. The umpires are ready, and Pakistan have spread out across the field, energized after a tight-knit pep talk from skipper Shan Masood. Ben Duckett and Zak Crawley are the openers for England. Aamer Jamal has the new ball in hand and will start proceedings for Pakistan! Away we go..
... THE SECOND INNINGS ...

Now, with the ball in their hands, Pakistan will know they must strike early to unsettle a formidable English batting lineup. The pitch has offered little assistance, but England will need to bat intelligently to establish a commanding first-innings total and build on their momentum. So sit tight, grab a coffee, and get ready, exciting phase awaits as the second innings is just moments away!

Mohammad Rizwan's scratchy stay came to an abrupt halt early on Day 2, having narrowly escaped a missed edge on Day 1. England’s bowlers showcased remarkable discipline, steadily wearing down the Pakistani lineup with crucial breakthroughs that thwarted any attempts to seize control. Although Salman Agha mounted a brilliant counterattack, pushing Pakistan past the 300-run mark, England remained unfazed, consistently claiming wickets to halt the flow of runs. Aamer Jamal and Noman Ali forged a determined 49-run partnership, demonstrating their resolve and holding firm through the first session. However, England rallied back strongly, ultimately wrapping up Pakistan's innings at 366. For England, Jack Leach remained the pick of the bowlers with 4 wickets while Brydon Carse got three against his name.

After opting to bat first, Pakistan found themselves on the back foot early, with Jack Leach making the new ball talk. The spinner struck twice in quick succession, removing opener Abdullah Shafique and the skipper Shan Masood, leaving Pakistan in a spot of bother. However, Saim Ayub and debutant Kamran Ghulam stepped up with resilience, stitching together a brilliant 149-run stand that brought some much-needed stability. Kamran looked composed throughout, bringing up a memorable debut Test century, while Saim fell just short of his own milestone, dismissed for a well-crafted 77.

What a remarkable effort from Pakistan's tail-enders to wag and frustrate England a bit longer! Their determination and grit made a significant impact, allowing the team to push their total to 366 runs. England will be delighted with their effort and with the momentum now in their corner, they’ll be eager to translate this energy into a solid performance with the bat.

Pakistan have been bowled out for 366!

Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the second session for the day! The umpires and players are all out in the middle. Noman Ali and Aamer Jamal will look to continue their good run in the middle for Pakistan! Brydon Carse will start with the ball for England! Here we go!
... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

Despite losing Mohammad Rizwan early on, Pakistan recovered well in this session. Salman Agha also couldn't make the most of his start, but it was the stand between Aamer Jamal and Noman Ali that got them back in the game. They played with a positive mindset and instead of blocking everything, their intent was to score runs which they did without taking many risks. The only setback for them was that Jamal looked a bit uncomfortable holding his hip on numerous occasions which is significant because he is their only pacer. That stand is now worth 49 runs and they will look to extend it further and get close to the 400-run mark while England will want to wrap things up as quickly as possible. Join us at 7.40 am GMT to catch all the exciting action in the second session!

It didn't take England long to get their first wicket of the day. Brydon Carse removed Mohammad Rizwan for 41 off 97 with Jamie Smith taking a fine catch behind the stumps. There was a little partnership brewing between Salman Agha and Aamer Jamal but Potts made the breakthrough while Jack Leach followed it up with another wicket quickly. However, things didn't go their way after that as Jamal and Noman Ali played admirably getting through some tough overs and also adding crucial runs to the total frustrating the English bowlers.

SESSION SUMMARY - 99 runs and 3 wickets in 27 overs! It would have been England's session but Pakistan have shown some great rearguard action taking their total over 350 runs. England were able to put early pressure on the hosts by checking the runs and picking up wickets at crucial times, but just let it slip in the second half of this session. The conditions are a bit overcast and the pitch is not doing much which are not good signs for the hosts as they have gone in with just one pacer. The English batters will enjoy playing here unless it drastically changes and starts to turn square.

Commentary.Commentary: All set for Day 2 to get underway! The two umpires make their way to the middle, followed closely by the English players, spreading out across the field. Mohammad Rizwan and Salman Agha stride out, ready to carry on from where they left off. The ball has been handed to Brydon Carse, who’s raring to kick off the day’s proceedings. Away we go!

Matthew Potts is up for a quick chat. He says that they need to work hard to break down the opposition's defense but he feels really great to lead the pace attack. Mentions that the partnership of Saim Ayub and Kamran Ghulam was well settled but their skipper, Ben Stokes did well to get a breakthrough. Ends up saying that the game is in a balance but today's set of play would be crucial for both sides.

PITCH REPORT - Nasser Hussain is down in the middle for the pitch report. He says that it surprisingly is cooler and cloudier in Multan than what they are used to. Adds that this technically being the Day 7 pitch, there are a lot of cracks but it looked considerably better than the Day 1 of the first Test. Mentions that the deck is still rock hard but the cracks have started to crumble where they meet. Mentions that the low bounce could be something to look for and says that Pakistan will look to get to around 350 runs and with 7 spinners in their squad they will want this pitch to turn more which could give them a big advantage. Concludes that if it doesn't spin, England will hold the upper hand.

On the flip side, England have done a tremendous job as well if we compare it with the first Day of the first Test match. Matthew Potts and Brydon Carse picked up two wickets in the first hour of the gameplay. The reverse swing deliveries have made some positive results in the first hour of Day 1. The spinning duo, Jack Leach and Shoaib Bashir have pressed the opposition with some turns and have got merit out of it as well. England also opted for the new ball after the completion of 80th over but so far they haven't got anything to knock the batters off the pitch. Will the middle order of the hosts live up to their expectations? or, will England be able to wrap the inning fast? Stay tuned as we gear up for a thrilling Day 2 of cricket, with the first ball just moments away.

Pakistan are in a comfortable position, thanks to the strong performance of Saim Ayub and Kamran Ghulam. They both notched a sturdy partnership on the board and Ghulam breached the 100-run mark on Day 1. By the end of the Day, they lost half of their team but were able to pile on 259 runs. The pitch is dry and slow as we expect from the tracks of Multan. Saim Ayub is in for a flash interview. He says that it was a difficult track to bat on with some balls keeping low and the turn on offer there. Adds that it seemed like a two-paced surface when the pacers were bowling. Feels that being focused at all times is important on such surfaces. Shares that the chat between him and Kamran Ghulam was to watch the ball and play according to the conditions. Tells that he is disappointed to not have gotten a bigger score.

So, who takes the first day? Well, Pakistan might seem ahead on the scoreboard. They managed to put up good runs on a comparatively slow and dying pitch. But England fought hard too. Their fast bowlers kept creating chances, interrogating the batters every now and then. The spinners, in contrast, had it rough though - the pitch didn't help them much. England's fielding was another big plus. England's bowling and fielding efforts kept them competitive and might feel they did enough to send half of the opposition into the hut. For Pakistan, the standout performer was Kamran Ghulam. He came to the crease very early, in the 11th over itself, and showed remarkable resilience, reading the situation with a good temperament.

With the second new ball taken, the English pacers were summoned back to create inroads, but that crucial breakthrough remained elusive. A short burst for Shoaib Bashir then, as the day drew to a close, provided a ray of hope for England as he removed the centurion Ghulam. Rizwan, first rusty, got accustomed and saw his team through the day, remaining unbeaten on 37.

England opened the session with pace bowling, exploiting the aging ball's tendency for reverse swing on the deteriorating pitch. Brydon Carse and Matthew Potts skillfully utilized this movement, posing significant challenges to the batters. Carse's efforts eventually paid off with a breakthrough. Also, Pakistan could have been six wickets down had they opted for a review against an apparent edge that caught Rizwan off-guard.

Mohammad Rizwan lived on a knife's edge and was thoroughly interrogated by the pacers for his vulnerability but ticked along. Kamran Ghulam though, without any baggage, and filling in the big shoes of Babar Azam, displayed a real mixture of watchfulness and strokeplay. He eventually notched up his maiden Test century, punctuated by a few lusty blows as well and played a gem of a knock for his country before perishing on 118.

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the final session of the day. The two umpires and the English players have made their way out to the centre. England are starting with pace in the form of Matthew Potts. Potts to Kamran first up. Let's play...
... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

As we have seen throughout the series, the older the ball gets, the easier it becomes to bat, and this trend continued in the second session with significantly less spin on offer compared to the first. Given the slower nature of the surface, the pacers will need to work harder after Tea to capitalize on any reverse swing available. For Ghulam, it will be a matter of starting fresh, while Saud Shakeel, having faced just two balls, will aim to settle into his innings and build a solid partnership. There are 33 overs left in the day's play, and we should be able to get all of them in, with the option of extending play by an additional 30 minutes if needed. Do join us back at 10 am GMT for the third and final session of the day.

However, as the old ball began to reverse, Ben Stokes seized the opportunity to introduce pace from both ends, even bringing himself into the attack. This change unsettled Ghulam, who had been at ease against the spinners but suddenly looked less comfortable facing the reversing ball. Despite battling cramps, Ghulam persevered to see out the session. Unfortunately for Pakistan, Ayub's innings came to a tame end as he popped a catch straight to short mid-off in the penultimate over before Tea, bringing an abrupt conclusion to their impressive 149-run partnership.

England will head into the Tea break with a bit of relief after that late wicket, but despite the breakthrough, it’s Pakistan who took the honours in this session. 94 runs were scored in the session from 28 overs at a rate of 3.36 runs per over. Earlier, Saim Ayub and the debutant, Kamran Ghulam picked up right where they left off in the morning session, giving a solid account of themselves. They looked assured, especially against spin, managing to find the perfect balance between caution and aggression. Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the post-Lunch session, folks! The umpires are punctual to make their way out to the middle and so are the players of England who take their field positions. From 19/2, Kamran Ghulam and Saim Ayub have done well to hold onto their ends and will resume their innings. It will be Jack Leach (10-0-35-2) to resume the proceedings in the second session. Here we go!
... DAY 1, SESSION 2 ...

Well then, the first session of this second Test has flown by. The ball has spun and gripped well for the tweakers, on the first day itself. Although not an extravagant spin, just a bit of a purchase off the deck. Pakistan will be happy to have not lost any wickets further. They would want to build on in the second session as it is usually considered the best time to bat in Test cricket. While England's aim will be to break this partnership quickly after the break. Session 2 begins in 40 minutes, at 7.40 am GMT. Stay tuned.

As Ben Stokes is known for his instant change of plans, he shuffled the spinners and even introduced Joe Root as a floater to extract more spin and unsettle the Pakistan batters. But Saim and Ghulam didn't flinch and constructed a solid resilient 3rd wicket stand, adding 60 runs together and sailing without further blemish to the end of the session. Overall, the first hour belonged to England, and the next was dominated by Pakistan, making it even-stevens.

England's initial approach with seamers Matthew Potts and Brydon Carse yielded next to little movement off the pitch. Sensing the lack of assistance for pace early on, skipper Ben Stokes swiftly changed tack, bringing on his spin duo. The wicket, as predicted pre-match, offered a bit of turn, grip, and variable bounce. This tactical shift paid dividends almost immediately, with Jack Leach striking twice in quick succession to drag Pakistan on the back foot.

Facing early pressure, Saim Ayub partnered with debutant Kamran Ghulam to steady the ship. The pair navigated the spinning deliveries with caution and alert, preventing further casualties. Kamran Ghulam in particular, new to this flavor of cricket, showed good character and didn't look afraid to play the strokes against the spinners while Saim Ayub was solid in defense. The two kept the scorecard ticking at a sedate pace.

LUNCH, DAY 1 - Session Summary - 29 overs, 79 runs, 2 wickets. Quite fair to say, a shared session. Pakistan did lose two early wickets but the third wicket stand sailed them through to the end of the session. Pakistan won the toss and elected to bat on a pitch that looked vastly different from the first Test. Openers Abdullah Shafique and Saim Ayub started cautiously, trying to get a feel for the surface. However, the introduction of spin bowling quickly turned the tide, with Pakistan losing both Shafique and captain Shan Masood cheaply within the first hour.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the action to commence here in Multan. A sparse crowd is in on a Tuesday morning but it should build as the day progresses. There is not a cloud in the sky as the two umpires make their way out to the centre. They are followed by Ben Stokes and his men. It will be the left-hand right-hand combination of Saim Ayub and Abdullah Shafique to open the innings for Pakistan. Matthew Potts will kickstart proceedings with the red cherry. Potts to Shafique first up. Two slips and a leg slip in place to start with. Away we go...

PITCH REPORT - Michael Atherton is near the deck. He notes that the ground staff watered the surface two days ago and utilized two large fans at both ends to speed up the drying process. Atherton also mentions that the pitch was left open to dry yesterday, resulting in some cracks opening slightly, though they remain firm. He expects the pitch to play well for the first day or two.

England (Playing XI) - Zak Crawley, Ben Duckett, Ollie Pope, Joe Root, Harry Brook, Ben Stokes (C) (In for Chris Woakes), Jamie Smith (WK), Brydon Carse, Matthew Potts (In for Gus Atkinson), Jack Leach, Shoaib Bashir.

Pakistan (Playing XI) - Abdullah Shafique, Saim Ayub, Shan Masood (C), Kamran Ghulam (On debut) (In for Babar Azam), Saud Shakeel, Mohammad Rizwan (WK), Salman Agha, Aamer Jamal, Noman Ali (In for Shaheen Shah Afridi), Sajid Khan (In for Naseem Shah), Zahid Mahmood (In for Abrar Ahmed).
TOSS - Pakistan have won the toss and they will BAT first.

Pakistan’s home record in Tests now stands at 11 defeats since March 2022, with seven losses coming in their last nine games. And they will be itching to get a win and play for pride, in front of the home crowd. But they’re aware that the opposition is on a juggernaut. Will it be the same flat Multan road? Or will it assist the bowlers this time around? All will be answered as the toss and teams are up next shortly.

We find ourselves back at the familiar venue, on the very pitch that previously pushed bowlers to their limits under gruelling conditions. This is where Harry Brook's epic 317 and Root's historic 262 unfolded. But this time around, it remains to be seen how the pitch behaves. This has been confirmed already to throw a further spanner into the works. Meaning, that the ball might spin, grip and swing from the very outset, unlike the first Test.

England, as it’s their new norm now, announced its squad the previous day and they have made a couple of changes. Now, having recovered from the hamstring injury, their full-time skipper Ben Stokes is all in readiness to take the reins after a three-month hiatus from the longest format. He replaces Chris Woakes while Gus Atkinson has been rested and a like-for-like pacer, Matthew Potts has been swapped in the mix. The duo have played all the Tests since the start of their home season and hence, they are given a break. The rest of the XI remains intact including Duckett, who finds the place. He dislocated his thumb in the first Test, but he is fit and fine now.

England on the other hand are riding on the wave of tremendous confidence they gained from an emphatic win over the hosts. Now, with a 1-0 in this 3-Test match series, the tourists are aiming to replicate their performance from the previous game, well not with the ball, to be serious. Although, in the absence of their key speedsters Wood and Archer, England has smartly scouted and restocked itself with the next-gen of speedsters who can clock tempting speeds while maintaining good lines and lengths. Gus Atkinson has been in the ranks for a while now and has proved to be a crucial component, but it was the debutant Brydon Carse who impressed everyone with his accuracy and probing bowling.

While Pakistan are without three of their high-profile players now, with an account of current form and fitness, they have swapped some emerging talents. The bowling unit has been refined by the inclusion of seasoned spinners like Noman Ali and Sajid Khan, while uncapped players like Haseebullah Khan, Kamran Ghulam, and Mehran Mumtaz too, find a place in the mix. They now have the chance to showcase their skills against a formidable England side.

Pakistan, the home side might still be feeling the sting of a remarkable defeat by an inning. Despite being in a strong position, they couldn’t convert that into a win. Now, intending to turn things around, they have come up with a refined squad that boasts fresh energy with a blend of experience. But more importantly, they have left out key players. One, of course, has shocked the world - Babar Azam being sidelined for the remainder of the series. Not only Babar, for a fact, but also the likes of Shaheen Shah Afridi and Naseem Shah have been released from the squad. Fairly to say, they were highly ineffective - Babar with the bat, and the omission of the latter bowlers is because they were almost shadows of themselves with the ball.

In Test cricket, scoring more than 550 in the first innings and still ending up on the losing side is indeed a very rare phenomenon, but that’s how things panned in the series opener. A track where over 1600 runs were accumulated collectively, it really proved to be the graveyard for the bowlers in so many senses. As we return to this same venue, we extend a literally very warm welcome to our coverage of the second Test between Pakistan and England. The action will unfold once again at Multan Cricket Ground, promising immersive five days for the fans.
